examples.label: Enumerate valid users with the bash exploit-db script
Python variant against a SecLists username wordlist

notes: Valid-user oracle via sign-in/sign-up responses lets you build a target list before brute-forcing. GitLab locks accounts after ~10 failures, so enumerate first, spray sparingly.

recommended.note: Feed a valid low-priv account into the authenticated RCE.

name: GitLab - User Enumeration
description: Enumerates valid GitLab usernames (via the sign-up/internal endpoints) to build a target list. Sign-up may be open at /users/sign_up. Version is exposed at /help.

defense.why_it_works: GitLab returns different HTTP responses for existing vs non-existing usernames on registration and profile endpoints. Scripts exploit these differences to enumerate valid accounts for targeted credential attacks.
defense.prerequisites: Network access to GitLab instance. Open registration or public user profile pages (default in GitLab CE).
defense.impact: Valid username list for targeted brute-force. Identifies admin and developer accounts for higher-value targeting. Maps the organization's developer roster.
defense.detection: Rapid sequential GET/POST requests to /users/<username> or registration endpoint. GitLab production.log showing sequential probes. Rack::Attack rate-limit triggers if configured.
defense.artifacts: GitLab production.log (sequential /users/ requests) | Rack::Attack log (rate-limit triggers) | Web server access log (sequential user profile GETs)
defense.prevention: Enable Rack::Attack rate limiting in GitLab configuration. Disable public user profile visibility for non-logged-in users. Enable account lockout after failed login attempts.
defense.misconfiguration: GitLab instance is public with no rate limiting on user enumeration endpoints, and profile pages return distinct responses for valid vs invalid usernames.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# GitLab default -- public user profiles
# No rate limiting on /users/<username>
# config/initializers/rack_attack.rb not configured
defense.secure_config:
# gitlab.rb
gitlab_rails['rack_attack_git_basic_auth'] = {
  'enabled' => true,
  'maxretry' => 10,
  'findtime' => 60,
  'bantime' => 3600
}
# Admin Area: set Visibility to internal/private
